reasons: narrow: The exact \(h-1\) exponents silently require a retained factual-equivalent block, but \(\mathcal H\) is not augmented by \(\varnothing\). For \(h=2\), two contexts can share a nonfactual prefix, one can intervene at the next coordinate, and the other can remain natural, producing two necessary single-conjunction representatives, which exceeds \(3^{1/3}\). With a ternary alphabet and one live natural-world test, the joint transition has three necessary partition-plus-flag successors, which exceeds \(2^{1}\). Summing branching-block sizes only yields \(h\), giving the honest exact counts \(3^{h/3}\) and \((r+1)^h\). The downstream advertised compiler runtimes are unchanged because the first difference is a constant factor and the second is one factor \(r+1\), polynomial in the explicit input length.

As frozen, the separation conjunction mentions only \(A\) and \(B\), so exact normalization produces \(\{A,B\}\), not the declared \(\mathcal H_n^{\mathrm{sep}}=\{\varnothing,A,B\}\). Adding the factual atom \(S_{\varnothing}=0\) makes normalization retain exactly the declared three contexts. It is redundant on the fixed factual-zero fibre and therefore preserves every feasible history and the claimed separation.

A normalized conjunction may be empty or reduce to a truth constant, so its exact retained context set may be empty. The cardinality \(h=|\mathcal H|\) must therefore admit zero; the compiler proofs cover \(h=0\), while results explicitly quantified over positive \(h\) remain unchanged.

verdict.note: Accept all three approval items. Because H need not contain the factual context, the honest exact transition bounds are 3^(h/3) and (r+1)^h. The existing compiler displays remain valid asymptotically: the single-conjunction difference is the constant 3^(1/3), and the joint difference is one factor r+1, polynomial in explicit input size; the proposed proofs state these absorptions and cover h=0. Adding S_empty=0 is redundant on the fixed factual-zero separation fibre and makes normalization retain the declared three contexts. Changing h to nonnegative correctly covers empty/constant normalized inputs. Accept the DID-NOT-LAND single-theorem statement replacement as loss: it changes no claim, the required exponent correction is already in the landed proof, and its omitted direct dependencies are available transitively.
